scope: Selected cross-cutting ECC harness evidence, extended to inspect the full eval-harness library and example closure plus key agent, hook, and host-skill adapters and dependency/license metadata. This is not a deep review of the full multi-harness catalog.

limits: Recursive Git tree was complete (6,674 entries; not truncated), with no submodule or symlink entries; 46 binary-named assets were indexed but not fetched.

Deep review remains representative: the source has 327 canonical skill entries, 72 agents, 98 legacy commands, and many platform-specific mirrors/adapters. This continuation inspected all nine eval-harness library modules, its example/fixture closure, and selected adapters and validators.

The eval gate still unconditionally refuses candidate execution. The eval test suite was not executed or exhaustively read; static checks, replay, receipts, and an adversarial fixture are not OS containment or evidence of a completed score.
Hook validator/configuration code and schemas were reviewed, but most hook handlers and session/memory transitive runtime helpers remain indexed only.

The package lock has 304 package records; 301 declare SPDX license identifiers and three do not (entities, mdurl, punycode.js). Third-party license texts were not fetched or reviewed; no package was installed.
Root ECC materials are MIT; a separate nested MIT notice for context-and-decisions names Matt Pocock. Other nested notices and third-party obligations are not fully assessed.
No external link was followed. Credential-related evidence records environment-variable names only, never values; no source code was executed or enabled.
next: Review the complete canonical skill/agent catalog and map duplicates/adaptations across .agents, .claude, .cursor, .codex, .opencode, and other harness adapters; selected .agents copies were checked, but context-budget and agent-harness-construction mirrors were not found at their expected paths.

Review the remaining eval-harness tests and surrounding CLI/test dependencies before considering any offline behavior; candidate execution remains unavailable until independently verified OS containment exists.
Trace the complete hook graph and session/memory helpers before considering any hook runtime; the current pass covered validators and fingerprint sidecar logic, not the full runtime.
Inspect the install-modules registry, full MCP server configurations, package requirements, permissions, and credentials before any integration; do not follow unverified external references.
Resolve the three lockfile dependencies without license identifiers and review actual third-party license texts before adopting dependency-backed candidates.
